newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says it won't tolerate territorial violation.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says it won't tolerate territorial violation.

text.p: Cuba said on Thursday it would tolerate no violations of its airspace or territorial waters by Cuban exile groups who plan ceremonies next Monday on the anniversary of Cuba's shooting down of two exile-operated planes last year.
Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Marianela Ferriol, asked about the exiles' plans at a regular weekly news briefing, said Cuba's position on territorial violations was unchanged.
"We will not permit any violation," she said.

Asked if this meant Cuba might be prepared to use force if its territory were violated, Ferriol added: "We will take all measures necessary to prevent a violation of our airspace or territorial waters."

Cuban exile groups in Florida, where most Cuban Americans live, said last week their plans to mark the anniversary included sending planes to international waters between Cuba and Florida to drop wreaths over the site of the plane downings.
Cuban MiG fighters shot down two small Cessna planes operated by an exile group called Brothers to the Rescue on Feb. 24 last year, killing the four Cuban-American crew.
President Fidel Castro's government argued the planes were in Cuban airspace and ignored warnings to leave, and added Cuba had tolerated numerous such violations in recent years.
The incident sparked international outcry led by the United States.

Ferriol declined to say whether Cuban and U.S. authorities had discussed exile-organised anniversary events. However, she said that in Cuba's view it was up to the United States to stop any violations of Cuban territory.
Ferriol also said any activities by small, illegal dissident groups in Cuba itself to mark the plane downings would not be tolerated.
"Any sort of activity that tries to subvert the order of this country...has no place here," he said.

Ferriol noted that Feb. 24 has another significance in Cuba as the anniversary of the start of the second phase of Cuba's independence wars against Spain in 1895. The date is normally observed with reaffirmations of Cuba's independence and sovereignty.
